lines.say: Why do you get dizzy after heavy squats?
Why does this happen, number fourteen.
During a heavy rep, you hold your breath and brace. The pressure in your chest and belly shoots up.
That squeezes your big veins, so less blood flows back to your heart.
Then you stand up and breathe out. Your blood pressure drops for a moment, and your brain gets less blood.
Long sets of squats also pull lots of blood into your legs, which makes it worse.
The fix: breathe out between reps, don't hold your breath for the whole set, and stand still for a few seconds before you walk.
If you black out, or it keeps happening, get checked by a doctor.
Next: can you shout your way to more strength?
